texts.preamble: Ghyan Singh vs State on 6 September, 2017 Author: Chief Justice Bench: Chief Justice High Court Of Judicature For Rajasthan At Jodhpur S.B. Criminal Revision No. 356 / 1998 Ghyan Singh S/o Sh.Anada Ram, B/c Mali, R/o Pal House Ghantagahar, Jodhpur. (Accused in Central Jail, Jodhpur) ----Petitioner Versus State of Rajsthan.
texts.facts: 2. In view of the testimony of the Food Inspector who lifted the Chilli powder sample from the shop of the petitioner and even the testimony of DW-1 and DW-2, learned counsel for the petitioner concedes that purchase of the sample from the petitioner has been proved. The FSL report Exhibit P-12 establishes that the sample did not confirm to the prescribed standards.
texts.arguments: 4. But, the learned counsel for the petitioner prays for directions to be issued as was done by the Supreme Court in the decision reported as 1997 (9) SCC 101 N.Sukumaran Nair V/s Food Inspector. 4. Section 433 Cr.P.C. reads as under:- "433. Power to commute sentence.- The appropriate Government may, without the consent of the person sentenced, commute- (a) a sentence of death, for any other punishment provided by the Indian Penal Code; (b) a sentence of imprisonment for life, for imprisonment for a term not exceeding Ghyan Singh vs State on 6 September, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107369670/ 1 fourteen years or for fine; (c) a sentence of rigorous imprisonment, for simple imprisonment for any term to which that person might have been sentenced, or for fine; (d) a sentence of simple imprisonment, for fine." 5. In N.Sukumaran Nair's case (supra) the Supreme Court observed and directed as under:- "The offence took place in the year 1984. Under clause (d) of Section 433 of the Code of Criminal procedure, 'the appropriate government' is empowered to commute the sentence of simple imprisonment for fine. We think that this would be an appropriate case for commutation of sentence where almost a decade has gone by. On deposit of such fine, the State Government may formalise the matter by passing appropriate orders under clause (d) of Section 433 of the Code of Criminal Procedure." 6. I find that in a later judgment reported as 2004(5) SCC 721 Dayal Singh V/s State of Rajasthan the Supreme Court had (3 of 4) [CRLR-356/1998] observed as under:- "15. In the instant case it was not disputed that for the offence charged a minimum sentence of 6 months' rigorous imprisonment is prescribed by law. We are not inclined to modify the sentence by passing an order of the nature passed in N. Sukumaran Nair where this Court in exercise of its extraordinary jurisdiction imposed only a sentence of fine and directed the State to exercise its powers under section 433 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to commute the sentence of simple imprisonment for fine. 7. Noting the two earlier decisions, in the decision reported as 2009(12) SCC 646 State of Rajasthan V/s Jagdish Prasad the Supreme Court directed as under:- Ghyan Singh vs State on 6 September, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107369670/ 2
